fullText:
Summary: Dialog Axiata (DIAL.N0000) is a high-quality, high-dividend business, but the share price has run ahead of it. On your NAV rule it is heavily overpriced: at about Rs 42 it trades at 4.3x its NAV of Rs 9.68. NAV understates a telecom company, whose value comes from its network and customers rather than its book, so I relied more on cash flow, earnings and dividends. Those methods also put fair value at about Rs 31, so the price is about 37% above it. I’d buy at up to about Rs 26, and treat under Rs 23 as a strong buy. The price has risen from Rs 11.70 at the end of 2024 to Rs 46.10 at the end of June, so the strong earnings recovery is already priced in.

Price and key figures
Price: about Rs 42 on 26 October, from Simply Wall St. It last traded at Rs 46.10 on 30 June, after a Q2 range of Rs 30.10–48.40. Please check it live.
First half of 2026 (group, unaudited): revenue rose 9% to Rs 95.5bn and profit roughly doubled to Rs 19.3bn. EPS was Rs 2.10 against Rs 1.00.
Why profit doubled: gross margin rose to 56.8% from 51.8% (direct costs fell even as revenue grew), finance costs fell, and there was a Rs 0.5bn exchange gain, against a Rs 0.6bn loss last year.
Cash flow: operating cash flow rose to Rs 46.4bn. After capex, intangibles and lease payments, first-half free cash flow was about Rs 32bn.
Capex is rising: contracted capex jumped to Rs 16.9bn from Rs 6.3bn in December, and the segment notes show Rs 24.6bn of capex committed in the half (cash paid so far, Rs 10.7bn).
Methods
Method	Reading
NAV (Rs 9.68)	4.3x, overpriced on your rule, though NAV understates a telecom company.
Return on equity	34% over the last 12 months (2025: 23%, 2024: 16%, 2023: 30%, 2022: a loss).
P/E	12.5x trailing EPS of Rs 3.35. Year-end P/E: 13.2x (2025), 8.2x (2024), 3.7x (2023).
Dividends	About Rs 2.90 (FY25 final Rs 2.20, plus a Rs 0.70 interim proposed). That’s a 6.9% yield, with about 86% of profit paid out.
Free cash flow	About Rs 32bn in the first half, an annualised yield of about 11–12% on the market cap of roughly Rs 386bn, likely lower once higher capex is paid.
Debt	Net debt about Rs 62.5bn including leases. Net debt was 0.64x EBITDA at end-2025, and debt to equity 0.85x.
Free cash flow to equity DCF	Rs 26.5 / 42.2 / 55.8 across the cases, weighted Rs 40.2.
P/E method	Rs 28 / 40 / 52, weighted Rs 38.7.
Dividend model	Rs 18.7 / 26.4 / 32.4, weighted Rs 25.0.
Residual income	Rs 14.3 / 19.3 / 23.6, weighted Rs 18.6.

Unlike the banks and conglomerates, Dialog suits a cash-flow DCF, because its cash generation is steady and not tied to lending. It’s the most generous method because the base case assumes capex doesn’t eat into free cash flow. Residual income is the strictest because it depends on today’s very high ROE, which I assume fades.

Assumptions
	Bear	Base	Bull
Normalised free cash flow to equity, 2026	Rs 32bn	Rs 42bn	Rs 48bn
Growth over 5 years, then long-term	2–3%, then 4%	6–7%, then 5%	7–10%, then 6%
Return on equity path	30% falling to 20%	34% falling to 25%	36% falling to 30%
2026 EPS × P/E	3.5 × 8	4.0 × 10	4.3 × 12
Dividend per share, growth	Rs 2.40, 2%	Rs 2.90, 6%	Rs 3.30, 8%
Average of the four methods	Rs 21.9	Rs 32.0	Rs 40.9

Common: cost of equity 17% (Sri Lankan bonds yield about 13%, plus a lower premium for a defensive telecom). In the base case, second-half EPS stays near the first half’s level, giving about Rs 4.0 for 2026.

Fair value and buy price
Fair value: weighting 30/50/20 gives about Rs 31 (3.2x NAV), so Rs 42 is about 37% above it.
Buy price: a 15% margin of safety gives Rs 26, and 25% gives Rs 23.
Plan for 500 shares: 200 at up to Rs 28, 150 at up to Rs 26 and 150 at up to Rs 24. That averages about Rs 26.20, about Rs 13,100, against Rs 21,000 at Rs 42.
Realism: the low this year was Rs 30.10 (Q2). Rs 26 would need about a 38% fall, which may not happen. If you want income now, a small starter near Rs 32–35 still yields about 8–9%, but with little margin of safety.
Sensitivity (DCF base case, Rs per share)
Cost of equity	Long-term growth 4%	5%	6%
15%	47.5	50.7	54.7
17%	40.1	42.2	44.7
19%	34.6	36.1	37.8

The DCF alone supports the current price only if you accept a cost of equity of 17% or less and the base cash flows.

What would change my view

Supports a higher value

Margins of about 55%+ holding in the second half.
The 5G rollout lifting revenue faster than capex.
Dividends of Rs 3+ a year being sustained.
Lower interest rates, which would lower the cost of equity.
Q3 results (to September, due by mid-November) confirming the first half. Upload them if they’re out.

Supports a lower value

Capex eating free cash flow: contracted capex nearly tripled, so dividends may be cut.
One-offs: the exchange gain and cost savings not repeating.
Tax and regulation: telecom levies, VAT changes or spectrum costs.
Price competition in mobile and broadband.
The rupee: network equipment is imported, and the company booked a Rs 1.4bn exchange loss in 2025.
Valuation risk: after a near-quadrupling since 2024, sentiment can reverse sharply, as it did in 2022, when the company made a loss.

These are my estimates from your annual report and interims. The interim figures are unaudited, and the price is from a late-October snapshot, so check it before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.
